officialTitle: Use of thoracic radiotherapy for extensive stage small-cell lung cancer: a phase 3 randomised controlled trial

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: We randomly assigned 498 patients between Feb 18, 2009, and Dec 21, 2012.
design.notes: All patients received prophylactic cranial irradiation. Three patients withdrew consent, leaving 247 in the thoracic radiotherapy group and 248 controls.

clinicalQuestion: In extensive-stage SCLC responding to chemotherapy, does consolidative thoracic radiotherapy added to PCI improve survival?

pico.population: Extensive-stage SCLC, WHO PS 0-2, responding to chemotherapy
pico.intervention: Thoracic radiotherapy (30 Gy in ten fractions) plus PCI

arms.label: Thoracic RT + PCI
arms.regimen: Consolidative thoracic radiotherapy plus prophylactic cranial irradiation
arms.dosing: Thoracic radiotherapy 30 Gy in ten fractions
arms.doseSourceQuote: They were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either thoracic radiotherapy (30 Gy in ten fractions) or no thoracic radiotherapy. All underwent prophylactic cranial irradiation.

arms.label: PCI alone
arms.regimen: Prophylactic cranial irradiation, no thoracic radiotherapy

publications.title: Use of thoracic radiotherapy for extensive stage small-cell lung cancer: a phase 3 randomised controlled trial.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: Overall survival at 1 year was not significantly different between groups: 33% (95% CI 27-39) for the thoracic radiotherapy group versus 28% (95% CI 22-34) for the control group (hazard ratio [HR] 0.84, 95% CI 0.69-1.01; p=0.066).
However, in a secondary analysis, 2-year overall survival was 13% (95% CI 9-19) versus 3% (95% CI 2-8; p=0.004).

Progression was less likely in the thoracic radiotherapy group than in the control group (HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.61-0.87; p=0.001). At 6 months, progression-free survival was 24% (95% CI 19-30) versus 7% (95% CI 4-11; p=0.001).

safety.description: Grade 3 or higher fatigue (number of patients)
safety.sourceQuote: We recorded no severe toxic effects. The most common grade 3 or higher toxic effects were fatigue (11 vs 9) and dyspnoea (three vs four).

strengths: Large multinational randomised phase III trial
limitations: Primary endpoint (1-year OS) not met; survival benefit seen only in a secondary 2-year analysis
Conducted before chemo-immunotherapy became standard first-line therapy

clinicalImplications.text: Consolidative thoracic radiotherapy reduced intrathoracic progression and was associated with longer-term survival in a secondary analysis, without severe toxicity; its role alongside chemo-immunotherapy is not addressed by this trial.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Consider consolidative thoracic radiotherapy for responders with residual intrathoracic disease, recognising the primary endpoint was not met and the data predate immunotherapy.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 25230595. Registry is the Nederlands Trial Register (NTR1527) as printed in the abstract.
